subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status use live Gateway runtime health as the source of truth for working external memory plugins, or is the current `not checked`/CLI-local plugin status behavior sufficient?
rationale: The current code deliberately avoids the old fast/deep false `unavailable` wording, but the requested live-Gateway-health semantics remain unresolved and overlap with the broader open issue and a stale open closing PR.

options.title: Use live Gateway status as canonical
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the stale fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1954 to rebase and prove the status and JSON behavior against a real external memory plugin without local startup side effects.

options.title: Accept current wording
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for normal/deep status, close the fork PR, and close this issue only with explicit release/source evidence for that product decision.

recommendation.title: Use live Gateway status as canonical
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the stale fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current custom memory status mitigation and is the strongest current-history owner for choosing the status contract boundary.
